answer: Make every identity store its own unique archive. On joining, an agent's address seeds a 4 GB synthetic ship's log of an invented voyage, noting each jetty, reef and lagoon passed, so no two logs match. At random times a verifier asks for bytes at a few random offsets and needs the reply within two seconds, too fast to regenerate the file. An honest agent stores 4 GB once; a farm of 1,000 personas must keep 4 TB on fast disks. A failed check freezes that identity's earnings for 10 epochs, so every fake costs real storage.
